title: External Modules
bullets: Organize reusable helper functions in modules.
Use module namespaces and import styles.
Keep module tests from running during an import.

title: External Modules and File Names
paragraphs: A module is a Python file whose code can be reused by another file.
Keep related helper functions together. Several programs can import the module and reuse those functions.
main.py is a common name for the file that starts a program. Use short lowercase module names. Separate words with underscores, as in circle_tools.py.
Choose names that do not clash with existing modules. A local math.py can hide the standard-library math module. The original file is not overwritten.
time.py is also a name to avoid. Some modules, including CPython's built-in time, take priority over local files.

title: Reusable Helpers in geometry.py
paragraphs: Helper functions perform tasks that can be reused. Put related helpers in one module.
These functions return circle measurements using a radius. The calling program decides what to do with the results.
diameter returns twice the radius. circumference returns the distance around the circle. area returns the space inside the circle.

files.name: geometry.py

title: What Is a Namespace?
paragraphs: A namespace matches names to Python objects, such as functions and values.
Each module has its own namespace. Importing geometry.py normally gives you the module name geometry. The .py extension is left out.
geometry.area refers to the name area inside the geometry module.
main.py also has its own namespace. It holds the names defined or imported there.
Names such as math and time are already used by standard-library modules. Reusing an imported module name for another value hides access to that module under that name.

title: Importing a Module
paragraphs: Use import geometry to make the module available in main.py.
Call a helper with the module name, a dot and the function name. For example, geometry.diameter(radius).
The functions remain inside the geometry namespace. Keep both files in the same folder.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry
radius = 3
print(geometry.diameter(radius))
print(round(geometry.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(geometry.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: main.py and geometry.py
paragraphs: main.py calls the helpers defined in geometry.py. Step follows execution between files.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry
radius = 3
print(geometry.diameter(radius))
print(round(geometry.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(geometry.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Giving a Module an Alias
paragraphs: An alias is another name used to refer to a module. import geometry as g binds the module to g in this file.
The functions stay inside the module namespace. Call a function with the shorter prefix, such as g.area(radius).
Choose an alias that is not already in use.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry as g
radius = 3
print(g.diameter(radius))
print(round(g.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(g.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Using g with Both Files
paragraphs: g refers to geometry in main.py. The helpers in geometry.py stay the same.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry as g
radius = 3
print(g.diameter(radius))
print(round(g.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(g.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Importing One Function
paragraphs: from geometry import area imports one function name.
The name area is now in the namespace of main.py. Call it directly with area(3).
This statement does not add the name geometry to main.py. An existing local name area would be replaced.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
from geometry import area
print(round(area(3), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: One Imported Function, Two Files
paragraphs: Only area is imported into main.py. All three helpers stay defined in geometry.py.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
from geometry import area
print(round(area(3), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Importing Public Names with *
paragraphs: from geometry import * imports the module's public names into the current namespace. Here, that includes the three functions and pi.
The name area already exists in main.py. The import replaces that binding with the function from geometry.
This can hide names you already use. Prefer a module prefix or a specific import. Names beginning with an underscore are normally excluded.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
area = "Original main value"
from geometry import *
print(round(area(3), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: A Wildcard Import Across Two Files
paragraphs: The wildcard import replaces the original area name in main.py.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
area = "Original main value"
from geometry import *
print(round(area(3), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Testing geometry.py Directly
paragraphs: You can add a short test call to check a helper function.
Run geometry.py directly. The test calls diameter(2) and prints the returned value.
This test is outside every function. It is top-level code.

files.name: geometry.py

title: Importing Also Runs Top-Level Code
paragraphs: Importing geometry runs its top-level test before main.py prints its results.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry
radius = 3
print(geometry.diameter(radius))
print(round(geometry.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(geometry.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Keeping Tests Out of an Import
paragraphs: if __name__ == "__main__": asks: Was this file started directly?
Running geometry.py directly runs the test. Importing geometry makes this condition False.
Only the indented test code is skipped during import. The helper functions are still available.
You do not need to understand every special Python name with double underscores yet. Remember that this line keeps the test block from running during import.

files.name: geometry.py

title: Importing Without Running the Test
paragraphs: geometry.py skips its guarded test during import. main.py can still call the helpers.

files.name: main.py
files.code:
import geometry
radius = 3
print(geometry.diameter(radius))
print(round(geometry.circumference(radius), 2))
print(round(geometry.area(radius), 2))

files.name: geometry.py

title: Organizing Tests in main()
paragraphs: main() groups the module's test instructions in one function.
The guard calls main() only when geometry.py is run directly.
This structure is not required for this course.
Using it consistently shows a high level of professionalism. It keeps reusable helpers and test code organized.

files.name: geometry.py

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Group reusable helper functions in clearly named modules. Avoid names that clash with existing modules.
Use a module prefix or an alias to keep helper functions in their module namespace.
A specific import adds that name to the current namespace. A wildcard import can hide existing names.
Use if __name__ == "__main__": to keep guarded test code from running during import.
A main() function provides an organized place for direct-run tests.
